3000: Section 3000 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual provides an overview of general program policies related to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). It addresses specific policy topics such as confidentiality laws governing case information, voter registration procedures mandated since January 1995, mandated reporting protocols for child abuse and neglect, and compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act to ensure non-discrimination. The section also details verification methods required for eligibility determination. This section does not cover income thresholds or resource limits, which are found in Section 4000. Caseworker inquiries about the program's purpose, voter registration requirements, and reporting obligations are addressed here, but questions regarding eligibility and budgeting calculations should be referred to their respective sections.
3005: Section 3005 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual covers the confidentiality requirements for information regarding Food Stamp Program applicants and recipients. Key topics include restrictions on disclosures to authorized entities related to program administration, emergencies, and certain legal and research situations. It outlines that any release of information without the applicant/recipient's consent must directly support administration of the FSP or other means-tested federal assistance programs. Notable terms include "A/R" for applicant/recipient and reference to O.C.G.A. 49-4-14 as the legal basis for confidentiality. Discussions on unauthorized data sharing highlight potential misdemeanor charges. This section does not address public records requests under section 4200 or employment verifications found under section 3105. It assists caseworkers with questions about permissible data sharing, but does not cover procedures for providing general, non-identifiable statistics.
3010: Section 3010 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on Voter Registration requirements aligned with the National Voter Registration Act of 1993 (NVRA) and Georgia law. It mandates the distribution of Voter Registration Application forms and Voter Registration Information at application, recertification, change of address, and upon customer request. The section outlines forms to be used, such as Forms 297, 298, 508, 846, 94, 94A, and 700, ensuring they include voter registration information. Caseworkers must document responses in the Gateway worker portal and mail completed applications to the Secretary of State’s Office. It prohibits influencing voter registration decisions and mandates confidentiality of personal information, aligning with public assistance confidentiality laws. This section does not cover processes unrelated to voter registration, such as general election procedures (refer to Section 3020 for those). Caseworkers can address questions about the voter registration process linked to SNAP, Medicaid, and TANF, but not broader electoral process inquiries.
3020: Section 3020 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual mandates that all DFCS employees report suspected child abuse or neglect, as per Georgia Code Section 19-7-5. Key decision points include recognizing signs of abuse, documenting observations, and making timely referrals to Child Protective Services (CPS) via a phone call followed by written documentation, using Form 713 when necessary. The section emphasizes anonymity for the reporter when requested and outlines the cooperative role of the Office of Child Advocate, including compliance expectations and notification procedures involving DFCS Legal Services. Procedures for making a CPS referral are clearly outlined, from initiating the county contact to maintaining documentation in the Gateway system. This section does not cover non-related reporting obligations, such as elder abuse reporting, which would be found in a separate section. Caseworker questions answered here involve reporting procedures and documentation for child abuse, while questions about the investigation process itself or handling confidentiality beyond the scope of CPS referrals need other resources or sections.
3025: Section 3025 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the adherence to the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act by the Georgia Department of Human Services and its Division of Family and Children Services (DHS/DFCS). Key policy topics include ensuring non-discrimination on the basis of disability and providing reasonable modifications and communication aids for qualified constituents. Forms such as the Reasonable Modification and Communication Assistance Request Form (Form 101) are instrumental in documenting requests, while denial of modifications is decided by the DHS/DFCS Division Director. Notably, this section applies to programs under DHS/DFCS' Office of Family Independence (OFI) and excludes matters related to child welfare and DHS employment, which are covered in other sections like DHS OHR Policy 1704. This policy section answers caseworker questions regarding procedural requirements for processing disability-related requests but does not cover employment-related ADA provisions.
3030: Section 3030 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses Civil Rights policies, mandating compliance with laws prohibiting discrimination based on race, color, national origin, age, sex, disability, and retaliation for prior civil rights activities. Key requirements include nondiscrimination in DHS/DFCS programs, the right to file civil rights complaints, requesting reasonable modifications, and public notifications. Notably, this section includes forms such as the DFCS Civil Rights, ADA/Section 504 Complaint Form 724 and the DFCS Reasonable Modification and Communication Assistance Request Form 101. It specifies training requirements and data collection protocols. Caseworkers can use this section to address discrimination complaints and reasonable modification requests but should refer to other sections, like DHS OHR Policy 101 and 102, for employment and sexual harassment issues, and DHS LEP/SI Policy 2001 for language assistance services.
3035: Section 3035 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the verification process required for initial applications, recertifications, and periodic reports. Key policy topics include verification of identity, citizenship, immigrant/alien status, gross income, and utility expenses, among others. The section outlines the use of Third-Party Sources (TPS) and the Assistance Unit's statement (AUS) as verification methods, detailing scenarios where each is applicable. Important tools and references include the Summary Verification Chart (Chart 3035.1), Verification Checklist (Form 173), and specific program interfaces like EIVS and IEVS. Notably, this section excludes guidance on computer match policies, which are detailed in Section 3500 and related subsections, and detailed citizenship eligibility for aliens, covered in Section 3320. Caseworker questions this section can answer include what verification is necessary at each stage of the application process, timelines for submission, and handling of questionable information. However, it does not cover procedural discrepancies for situations specifically involving fraud investigations, which should be referred to OIG protocols.
3040: Section 3040 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual delineates the requirements for compliance with the Health Information Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) of 1996, covering security and privacy of Protected Health Information (PHI). Key policy topics include the Privacy Rule, Notice of Privacy Practices, and the Security Rule, with forms like Form 5460 and Form 5459 highlighted for mandatory use. The section outlines specific situations requiring or exempting the need for individual authorization for PHI disclosure, emphasizing the "Minimum Necessary" standard and administrative requirements. It also lists scenarios not covered here, such as TANF eligibility (refer to Section 3030) or Medicaid-specific regulations, which belong in separate sections. This section answers questions on HIPAA compliance, covered entities, and authorization processes, but does not cover non-health-related confidentiality issues or other program-specific confidentiality requirements.
3100: Section 3100 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the application process, beginning with the request for SNAP benefits and ending with eligibility notification to the Assistance Unit (AU). It clarifies that applications must be available upon request and can be submitted through various methods, including in person, by mail, phone, or electronically. The section mandates verification of citizenship, immigration status, and SSN for those applying for benefits while allowing non-applicants within an AU not to provide these verifications; however, their income and resources are still considered for eligibility calculations. Key rules include timely processing of applications and expedited screening for applicants. This section does not cover definitions of Assistance Units (see Section 3205) or specific eligibility criteria for SNAP benefits. It can answer questions related to application submission methods and verification requirements but does not address eligibility details or AU composition definitions.
3105: Section 3105 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the application processing for SNAP benefits. It outlines the entire application process, including the filing and completion of applications, verification, interviews, and processing within the Standard of Promptness (SOP). Key topics covered include the Right to Same-Day Filing, cooperation requirements for the AU, application withdrawal, expedited screening, and the process for mandatory interviews. Important forms such as Form 297 (Application for Benefits) and Form 297A (Rights and Responsibilities) play a crucial role. It emphasizes the 30-day SOP for non-expedited applications and the 7-day standard for expedited cases. The section includes charts (3105.1 and 3105.2) for assigning certification periods and application filing procedures. This section does not cover detailed policies on authorized representatives (see Section 3120) or changes in the head of the AU designation (see Section 3715). Caseworker questions about the SNAP eligibility determination, interview scheduling requirements, and application processing steps are addressed here. However, questions on SNAP E&T Program referrals and reporting changes should be referenced to specific sections such as Section 3110 and Section 3710.
3110: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual, 3110, focuses on expedited application processing for the SNAP program. It outlines the criteria under which an Assistance Unit (AU) may qualify for expedited services, particularly emphasizing financial thresholds such as having less than $150 in income and not more than $100 in liquid resources. Key forms and tools, such as the expedited screening tool (Form 296) and SNAP Screening and Referral Tool (Form 864), are identified for application processing. The section mandates that benefits be issued by the 7th day following application if eligibility is determined. It further specifies that interviews may be required and must be completed within certain time frames to maintain expedited status. Noteworthy conditions that do not belong here include cases involving work sanctions (Sections 3355 and 3380) or those receiving benefits in another state (Section 3510). This section answers questions on eligibility verification, expedited processing time limits, and certification periods but does not cover general certification processes or out-of-state benefit issues.
3115: Section 3115 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses special considerations for processing SNAP applications, particularly focusing on applications submitted by households where all members are either applying for or receiving SSI. It outlines that such households can apply for SNAP at the SSA office and includes a decision chart (Chart 3115.1) detailing that the date of application is marked as when the SSA office receives it. Additionally, eligibility for expedited processing begins immediately upon receipt. It specifies that complete applications should be processed without further contact, while incomplete ones require follow-up. For joint TANF/SNAP or GA/SNAP applications, a single interview suffices if the household opts to apply for both, with expedited SNAP processing proceeding if immediate interviews are not possible. This section does not address situations where interviews must be conducted at the SNAP office for these cases (see Section 3220). It provides clear guidance on processing applications and joint application procedures but does not address detailed eligibility criteria for SSI or GA benefits themselves.
3120: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the requirements and procedures for designating an Authorized Representative (AR) for a Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) assistance unit (AU). Key policy topics include the eligibility criteria for ARs, which can be adults familiar with the AU's circumstances or employees of specific community organizations, and conditions under which certain individuals may serve as ARs with county director approval. Important terminology and thresholds include the documentation requirements for designating an AR, such as written statements or release forms, and verification of the AR's identity. Notably, caseworkers should refer to Section 3220 for policies pertaining to drug and alcohol treatment centers acting as ARs. This section addresses questions about who may be designated as an AR, what roles they can fulfill, and the process for disqualification, but it does not provide guidance on the application process itself, which is covered in a different section.
3125: Section 3125 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual covers the Disaster Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (DSNAP), detailing eligibility criteria, application processes, and benefit issuance for households impacted by disasters. Key eligibility requirements include living or working in the disaster area, experiencing adverse effects such as loss of income, and meeting adjusted income and resource criteria. The section specifies that existing SNAP recipients cannot receive DSNAP in the same month and outlines steps for determining net income, accessible resources, and disaster-related expenses. Important forms and time limits include pre-registration (Form 854), a 3-day standard of promptness for application processing, and specific gross income limits per household size as shown in a detailed chart. This section does not address citizenship status, work requirements, or IPV disqualifications which are covered by other sections. Caseworker inquiries resolved here may include DSNAP eligibility determination and application processes, while those requiring clarification on regular SNAP rules or other program exceptions should refer to relevant sections like 3120 for authorized representatives.
3200: Section 3200 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the composition and eligibility criteria for Assistance Units (AUs), which consist of individuals receiving benefits upon application approval. The AU size is critical as it sets the income limit, and all members' income and resources are evaluated for eligibility. Importantly, income and resources from certain financially responsible individuals, who are not included in the AU, are also considered. Caseworkers should refer to this section for guidance on determining AU composition and eligibility criteria, including size and financial assessments, but not for allocation of benefits or sanction policies, which are covered in Section 3300. This section does not include specific forms, thresholds, or time limits, as these are covered in specialized sections related to eligibility verification and resource assessment.
3205: Section 3205 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual provides detailed guidelines for determining the composition of a Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Assistance Unit (AU). It specifies criteria such as living arrangements, shared meal preparation, and specific relationships like spouses and parental control that determine AU inclusion. Additionally, it outlines exclusions for individuals disqualified due to issues like IPV, sanctions, and certain criminal convictions. Notable resources include Chart 3205.1, which aids in determining AU composition, and Appendix A for financial standards. It also clarifies the treatment of specific member categories such as boarders, live-in attendants, and institutional care residents. Caseworkers will find guidance on AU composition but should refer to Section 3600 for budget considerations for excluded members and to Section 3220 for residents in treatment centers.
3210: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual, Section 3210, details the conditions under which households are categorically eligible for SNAP benefits, specifically those receiving TANF, Work Support Payments (WSP), Supplemental Security Income (SSI), or TANF Community Outreach Services (TCOS). It outlines that categorical eligibility begins when all assistance unit (AU) members are certified for TANF cash assistance, WSP, or SSI and continues even if benefits are recouped or suspended. The section emphasizes that TCOS eligibility involves evaluating income at or below certain federal poverty levels. Key requirements and forms include the Application for Benefits - Form 297, Form 297A, and the SNAP/Medicaid/TANF Renewal Form 508. Notably, households are not categorically eligible if they include an IPV disqualified member, or if they transfer resources to qualify for benefits, with potential exceptions outlined. While the section provides detailed eligibility criteria and exceptions for TANF, WSP, SSI, and TCOS-related categorical eligibility, it does not address IPV disqualification processes (refer to Section 3240) or standard SNAP eligibility requirements unlinked to these categories. Caseworkers can use this section to determine categorical eligibility based on assistance programs but must refer to other sections for broader eligibility issues, like verifying IPV disqualifications or specific AU composition rules.
3215: Section 3215 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines eligibility criteria and procedures for residents of battered women and children shelters applying for SNAP benefits. It covers policy topics such as designating an authorized representative, dual participation in assistance units, and the inaccessibility of jointly-owned resources. Key procedures include verifying the shelter’s SNAP approval status, assessing the resident's certification in other assistance units, and prorating benefits from the application date. The section requires shelters to be publicly operated or nonprofit entities with a designated area for battered women and children and mandates FNS authorization if SNAP benefits are exchanged for meals. This section cannot address scenarios involving shelters that do not meet SNAP definitions (see Section 3210) or cases where family violence issues don't result in shelter residency (refer to Section 3220). It clarifies caseworker queries about eligibility determinations specific to battered shelter residents but does not pertain to other non-custodial parent cases or unauthorized shelter facilities.
3220: Section 3220 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual covers the eligibility criteria and procedures for residents of drug and alcohol treatment centers to receive SNAP benefits. Key topics include the role of an authorized representative in applying for and receiving benefits on behalf of the residents; the criteria treatment facilities must meet to be recognized as SNAP-authorized retailers or licensed as tax-exempt organizations; and the procedure for handling SNAP benefits and EBT cards when residents leave the facility. Notable conditions include that this section does not cover policies for non-resident participants of treatment programs (see Section 3205). Forms or terminology such as the SNAP Authorization Permit, EBT card, and authorized representative are central to understanding compliance. This section answers caseworker questions on resident eligibility, facility certification, and the handling of SNAP benefits for residents but does not address eligibility for non-residents or institutions not certified by the Department of Behavioral Health and Developmental Disabilities.
3225: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the eligibility requirements and application procedures for disabled and blind individuals residing in group living arrangements, such as personal care homes. It covers the various ways residents can apply for benefits, including using an authorized representative. Key requirements include obtaining non-profit tax status, certification by DCH/HFR, and serving between two and sixteen residents. Facility responsibilities include maintaining a SNAP recipient list and managing EBT accounts in case of authorized representative changes. The section details budgeting procedures for resident income, including room/board and personal allowance supplements and distinguishes shelter and medical expenses for deductions. Notably, this section does not cover eligibility for residents of larger institutional settings (see Section 4000 for institutional eligibility policies). Caseworkers can use this section to determine eligibility and benefit levels for qualified group living residents but should refer to other sections for rules on institutional care or non-group living eligibility criteria.
3230: Section 3230 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses eligibility for individuals residing in homeless shelters. It specifies that individuals without a fixed nighttime residence who live in supervised or halfway houses can qualify for SNAP benefits. The section outlines the requirement for these individuals to meet the same eligibility and verification criteria as other Assistance Units (AUs). Key procedures involve accepting applications without an address, arranging alternate mailing addresses, verifying income and resources, applying standard deductions, and assigning a certification period not exceeding twelve months. Notably, residents of nonprofit shelters cannot be denied on the basis of institutional residency. This section directs caseworkers to Section 3205 for broader policies on homeless individuals and clarifies that the number of meals provided by the shelter is irrelevant to eligibility considerations.
3235: Section 3235 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the special treatment and criteria for migrant and seasonal farmworkers engaged in temporary agricultural work. Key rules include defining a farmworker AU as destitute if income sources are terminated or new, provided liquid resources don't exceed $100, and income is not received by specific deadlines. The section specifies processing guidelines, including expedited service eligibility and income calculations, such as excluding certain travel reimbursements. It highlights exemptions, like work registration and vehicle valuation, while utilizing specific terms like AU, destitute, and liquid resources. Conditions that trigger different rules, such as receiving income from the same employer, are defined elsewhere (e.g., Section 3110 and 3605). Caseworkers can use this section to determine eligibility and process applications for farmworker AUs but should refer to different sections for detailed income budgeting and expedited application procedures.
3240: Section 3240 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the eligibility of Assistance Units (AUs) with individuals involved in a strike, outlining specific rules and procedures for determining SNAP benefits. Key considerations include assessing pre-strike eligibility and ensuring strikers meet work registration requirements. Notably, this section specifies that AUs are not eligible for increased benefits due to income loss from a strike. Chart 3240.1 provides detailed steps for evaluating applications and ongoing cases, including comparing pre-strike and current income levels against Gross Income Cutoff (GIC) and net income tests. Individuals not considered strikers include those affected by lockouts, fearing personal injury, or exempt from work registration requirements for reasons other than employment. This section does not cover scenarios like voluntary employment changes unrelated to strikes; such cases might fall under employment change policies (see Section 3110). This section guides workers in assessing strikers' eligibility but does not address non-strike-related employment changes.
3245: Section 3245 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses eligibility requirements for students seeking SNAP benefits. It specifies that individuals aged 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in an Institution of Higher Education (IHE) must meet special criteria, such as employment status or participation in certain programs like TANF or work-study, to qualify. The section details exemptions based on age, physical or mental unfitness, and caregiving responsibilities, and clarifies that courses like English as a Second Language are not considered higher education. It mentions that Form 875 is used for verifying eligibility through work-study and highlights that students receiving the majority of their meals from an institution are ineligible. For educational income exclusions and specific policy on educational income, refer to Section 3420. Caseworkers can use this section to determine student eligibility criteria but not for general enrollment status guidelines, which remain in this document.
3300: Section 3300 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the non-financial eligibility criteria required for an Assistance Unit (AU) member to receive food stamp benefits. Key topics include the need for cooperation with eligibility investigations and adherence to FS work requirements, alongside criteria such as citizenship/alien status, enumeration, identity, and residency. Important terminology includes "Intentional Program Violations" and "Lawbreakers," which are crucial for understanding compliance. This section specifically addresses eligibility checks but does not cover financial eligibility metrics found in Section 3400 or benefits calculation, which is detailed in Section 3500. Caseworkers can use this section to verify if an AU member meets the basic non-financial criteria for further processing but cannot determine benefit amounts or financial eligibility requirements here.
3305: Section 3305 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the requirements for an Assistance Unit (AU) to cooperate with Quality Control (QC) reviews and the Office of Inspector General (OIG) investigations. AUs must cooperate with QC reviews, or face eligibility termination; refusal results in the eligibility worker (EW) closing the case after receiving written instructions from QC staff. Conversely, while an AU is requested to participate in OIG investigations of past eligibility, cooperation is not mandatory, and current benefits are unaffected unless current eligibility is questioned. This section includes actions required based on QC reviews, the non-mandatory nature of cooperation with OIG inquiries, and the administrative hearing process for adverse actions. It does not address termination procedures for refusal to cooperate with non-QC audits; see Section 3100 for eligibility determination protocols. Caseworkers can use this section to understand cooperation requirements with QC and OIG but should refer to other sections for procedures on initial benefits assessments and recertification eligibility.
3310: Section 3310 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the ineligibility criteria for lawbreakers, specifically focusing on individuals convicted of certain felonies, parole or probation violators, and fleeing felons. The section clarifies that individuals convicted of drug-related felonies after August 22, 1996, are no longer permanently disqualified from SNAP benefits, following the July 1, 2016, legislation change in Georgia. Key components include the Four-Part Test for determining fleeing felon status, the definition of "actively seeking," and agency response timelines of 20 to 30 days for confirming law enforcement action. It provides detailed procedures for disqualifying lawbreakers, specifying that caseworkers must document parole or probation statuses, verify with law enforcement if questionable, and provide adequate notice for disqualification actions. This section does not cover scenarios involving SNAP income calculation errors or benefits misuse by lawbreakers, which should refer to Section 3625. Caseworkers will find guidance on eligibility determinations related to felony convictions and compliance with legal conditions but will not find specific policy on first-offender status or minor legal considerations, which must be referenced elsewhere.
3315: Section 3315 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses Intentional Program Violations (IPVs), detailing disqualification criteria and periods for individuals committing IPVs. Key components include defining IPVs such as providing false information and trading SNAP benefits, and establishing how disqualifications are determined via court convictions or administrative findings like a Prosecuting Attorney's Consent (PAC) Agreement. Time limits for imposing disqualification are within 45 days of relevant court orders or agreements, as detailed in Chart 3315.1. It also covers eligibility of remaining household members, specifying that timely notice is not required but adequate notice is. Caseworkers are guided on entering disqualifications into the eDRS and handling disqualified individuals’ income/resources. This section does not address appeals or benefit restoration procedures; those are found in Section 3625.
3320: Section 3320 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses Citizenship/Alien Status, detailing eligibility requirements for SNAP benefits based on citizenship or alien status. It specifies the categories of individuals eligible for SNAP benefits, including U.S. citizens, Non-Citizen U.S. Nationals, Lawful Permanent Residents (LPR), and certain alien groups. Verification of citizenship or immigration status is necessary, with various acceptable forms listed. Notably, some exceptions exist for expedited processing or undocumented aliens, who are addressed separately in Section 3635. Charts 3320.1, 3320.2, and 3320.3 offer clear delineations of eligibility based on alien group status, especially pertinent with the enactment of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) from July 4, 2025, which alters some eligibility criteria. Caseworkers can refer to this section for guidance on verifying eligibility, understanding timelines for changes like OBBBA, and using the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) system. It does not cover budgeting processes, which are found in Section 3635.
3325: Section 3325 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual covers the enumeration requirements, including when and how Social Security Numbers (SSNs) should be provided by Assistance Unit (AU) members for SNAP benefits eligibility. It details the process of enumeration, the conditions under which an individual can be classified as a non-applicant, and the implications for benefits if a member fails to meet these requirements. The section outlines procedures for obtaining and recording SSNs using charts 3325.1 and 3325.2, establishes conditions for "good cause" exceptions, and specifies enumeration sanctions. Key deadlines include the 10-calendar-day period for providing SSNs or verification of SSN applications. This section can answer caseworker questions regarding enumeration requirements, timelines for applying for SSNs, and good cause justifications. However, questions related to recertification and changes beyond enumeration, such as eligibility determination without enumeration issues, should refer to Section 3620.
3335: Section 3335 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on verifying the identity of applicants and authorized representatives (AREP) applying for SNAP benefits. It references 7 CFR § 273.2(f)(1)(vii) for legal backing and outlines that both the applicant's and AREP's identities must be confirmed, either through documents or collateral contacts that reasonably establish identity. Suggested verification sources include documents like a birth certificate, driver's license, and voter registration card, but any document reasonably proving identity must be accepted, and no specific document type is mandatory. The section specifies that fraudulent or altered identity verifications lead to denial if unrectified, and a case review should be requested from the Office of Inspector General (OIG). Notably, collateral contacts are discouraged in fraud-suspected cases, and if more supportive documents are needed, caseworkers are encouraged to assist the applicant. This section does not cover procedures for non-identity-related fraud, which might be outlined in another section, and does not address how to verify financial eligibility, which could be found in Section 3340.
3340: Section 3340 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the residency requirements for Assistance Unit (AU) members. It specifies that AU members must reside in Georgia, although no specific duration of residency is required, and they may be homeless. Residency does not necessitate a fixed dwelling. While AUs are encouraged to apply in their resident county, they may apply and be certified in any county within the state. The section outlines acceptable forms of residency verification, such as documentation from the Georgia Department of Driver Services or other proof like utility receipts or a written statement from a responsible reference. At recertification, the AU's statement of continued residency is accepted unless conflicting information is present. This section does not cover scenarios related to residency disputes between counties, which are addressed in Section 3105. Caseworkers will find guidance on initial application residency verification but not on inter-county residency disputes or establishment of residency timelines.
3345: SECTION: 3345 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the SNAP Employment & Training (E&T) Work Requirement, specifically the SNAP Works Program. It outlines participation as voluntary for SNAP recipients and details the program’s objectives, such as promoting self-sufficiency, full-time employment, and collaboration with the business community and educational providers. The section discusses the administrative structure managed by the Department of Human Services, Division of Family and Children Services, emphasizing the role of case management in fostering self-sufficiency through individualized employment plans. Terminology in this section includes Individual Employment Plan (IEP) and case management process, with legislative authority stemming from the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 and the Balanced Budget Act of 1997. Notably, this section does not address the specific eligibility criteria for SNAP benefits (see SECTION 3100), nor does it cover the benefits issuance process (see SECTION 3600). Caseworker questions answered here include program objectives, case management responsibilities, and collaboration requirements; however, it does not address detailed eligibility guidelines or benefits calculation.
3350: Section 3350 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines work registration requirements for applicants and recipients, detailing criteria for work registration status, exemptions, and the responsibilities of work registrants. It covers the work registration process at initial application, interim changes, recertifications, and periodic reports, and describes exemptions based on age, physical or mental unfitness, student status, and caregiving responsibilities. Key forms mentioned include Form 859, SNAP Consolidated Work Requirements Notice, and notable thresholds involve employment hours and federal minimum wage. Charts 3350.1 and 3350.2 list work registration exemptions and categories of work registrants. This section does not cover eligibility for the SNAP Works Program, which is found in Section 3345, or compliance details for ABAWDs, which are in Section 3355. It addresses caseworker questions related to whether an applicant is subject to work registration or qualifies for exemptions but not questions about specific procedures for the SNAP Works Program.
3355: Section 3355 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the rules concerning Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs), particularly regarding the time limits and work requirements related to SNAP benefits. Key topics include the 36-month period rule, ABAWD Work Requirement exemptions, conditions for regaining eligibility, the ABAWD Waiver, and Discretionary Exemptions. Important forms and tracking tools include the Form 805, Form 859, and the ABAWD Tracking Calendar Form 507. Notably, ABAWD policies do not cover work registration specifics, which are detailed in Section 3350, nor do they address failure to comply with broader work requirements found in Section 3380. This section can help caseworkers assess eligibility, track compliance, and determine exemption or eligibility in terms of ABAWD status, but does not provide guidance on recertification specifics outside of ABAWD policies.
3360: Section 3360 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the requirements and procedures related to the E&T Participation Requirement within the SNAP Works program. It outlines the criteria to qualify as a SNAP Works eligible individual, stipulating mandatory conditions such as receiving SNAP assistance, fitness for employment, and voluntary program enrollment. Key responsibilities of the SNAP Works Program Employment Services Specialist (ES) include participant case management, documentation in the Georgia Gateway system, and notification of employment cases. The section specifies the conditions for positive and negative program completions, with accompanying codes and reasons, which are critical during case closures outlined in Chart 3360.1. This section does not cover eligibility for TANF recipients or students pursuing higher education degrees, as these scenarios are directed to other sections. Caseworker questions addressed include eligibility criteria for participation, required documentation, and the process for closing training activities, but not broader SNAP eligibility or non-E&T-related SNAP policies.
3365: Section 3365 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the E&T Enrollment Process, which is mandatory for all SNAP Works participants. It details the program orientation, employability assessments, and development of an Individual Employment Plan (IEP). Key components include understanding the program's purpose and requirements, assessing participants' educational and work backgrounds, and establishing employment goals with detailed steps and timelines. Information must be recorded in the Gateway system. This section does not address exemptions for participation, which might be covered under ABAWD policies in a different section (check relevant ABAWD sections). Questions a caseworker can answer include enrollment steps, documentation requirements, and development of an IEP, but not eligibility exemptions or nonparticipation penalties unless specified as good reasons.
3370: Section 3370 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses E&T (Education & Training) Participation Activities, detailing specific policy topics such as allowable components, participation requirements, and monitoring procedures. Key rules include the maximum participation limit of 120 hours per month and the 24-month limitation on education/training activities. Important terminology includes ABAWD (Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents) and SNAP Works Program components, categorized into education, work, and non-education/non-work types. Monitoring processes require E&T Providers and Employment Services Specialists to document participation through monthly reports. Notably, any questions regarding the specific criteria or involvement of SNAP participants as "work registrants" should refer to Section 3350. Caseworkers can use this section to determine eligibility and participation rules but should consult Section 3350 for student criteria not addressed here.
3375: Section 3375 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on Participant Support Services within the SNAP Works Program, outlining the reasonable and necessary work support services for program participation, including background checks, childcare, and transportation assistance. It details transportation assistance with an upfront payment of $25 for the first month, a monthly reimbursement of $50, and arranged transportation services up to $200. The section defines UAS Codes (such as 549 for Transportation Services) and Entitlement Codes, with guidelines detailed in Chart 3375.1. It emphasizes incidental support services like books and occupational licensing fees (Chart 3375.3) and prohibits the duplication of payments across programs. However, it does not address non-transportation or incidental services beyond referrals (e.g., to local resources). The section will not address unrelated support services, which are covered in separate areas of the manual, potentially found in other sections like those dealing with eligibility or entitlement calculation specifics. Caseworkers can find guidance on transportation assistance thresholds, incidental support limitations, and documentation requirements here, but not on unrelated benefits inquiries (which may be covered in sections such as 3345 or 3350).
3380: Section 3380 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the policies regarding failure to comply with work requirements for SNAP recipients, specifically highlighting the consequences and sanctions imposed on ABAWDs and mandatory registrants. This section outlines the general work requirements, conditions for good cause exemptions, and defines unsuitable employment, while detailing sanctions for violations as follows: a minimum of one month for the first violation, three months for the second, and six months for subsequent violations. Key forms mentioned include the SNAP Sanction/Penalty Notice form 333, and Chart 3380.1 specifies compliance methods for work requirements. Notable conditions where a work sanction is not imposed are when exemptions apply, good cause is determined, or compliance occurs before the sanction period begins. Caseworker questions related to determining compliance and sanctioning for non-compliance are addressed here, while questions regarding the policy application for general SNAP participation requirements should refer to Section 3385 as mentioned in the manual.
3385: Section 3385 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the implications of failing to perform required actions in means-tested public assistance programs, specifically TANF, and its impact on SNAP benefits. The section clarifies that SNAP benefits will not be increased if an Assistance Unit's (AU) income is reduced or terminated due to non-compliance with TANF requirements, such as providing a Social Security Number or failing to meet educational requirements for minor parents. Key tools include Chart 3385.1, detailing TANF requirements and corresponding consequences, and procedures for case workers on applying sanctions and budget assessments. This section explicitly excludes scenarios where TANF applications are denied for reasons other than failure to perform required actions or other procedural failures—these fall under Section 3380 regarding E&T work requirements compliance. Caseworkers can resolve questions related to the application of sanctions on SNAP benefits following a failure to comply with TANF requirements but must refer to other sections for issues concerning purely procedural failures or unrelated program terminations.
3400: Section 3400 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the financial eligibility criteria for SNAP benefits, focusing on resource and income limits. The section specifies resource limits of $4,500 for Assistance Units (AUs) with at least one member aged 60 or older or disabled, and $3,000 for other AUs, with certain exemptions for categorically eligible individuals such as TANF or SSI recipients. Income limits are based on the Federal Poverty Level (FPL), where most AUs are subject to a maximum gross income limit of 130% of the FPL, except for AUs with members aged 60 or older or disabled, who face a net income limit of 100% of the FPL. Key charts and tables, such as the Allotment and Proration Tables, are referenced in Appendix A. Caseworkers should note that this section does not cover eligibility aspects related to earned income deductions, found in Section 3210. This section answers questions related to resource and income thresholds but not those concerning non-financial eligibility criteria.
3405: Section 3405 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the policies regarding the assessment of resources for SNAP eligibility. It defines resources as assets accessible to the Assistance Unit (AU) that can be converted to cash for daily expenses and outlines the conditions under which resources are counted or excluded. The section includes specific resource limits ($4,500 for AUs with elderly or disabled members and $3,000 for all others), and questions to resolve during eligibility determination, such as resource accessibility and ownership. Notable resources include bank accounts, annuities, and real estate, with specific criteria for inclusion or exclusion, as detailed in Chart 3405.1. The policy also explains transfers of resources, commingling rules, and significant return values. "NOT HERE IF" conditions include policies regarding categorically eligible AUs found in Section 3210, Access to exemptions in the Trust category should be referred to Chart 3405.1, and rental properties guidance (Section 3425). This section assists caseworkers in determining the countability and value of resources, while exclusions involving categorically eligible AUs and income treatment fall outside its scope.
3415: Section 3415 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the treatment of real property in the determination of resources. It categorizes properties into homeplace, non-income producing, and income producing, detailing exemptions and inclusions, such as exempting a single homeplace and counting other buildings on the property. Key decision points include determining if the property produces income consistent with fair market value (FMV) and if it's subject to a good faith effort to sell. This section provides a chart, CHART 3415.1, detailing the FS treatment for various property types. It excludes scenarios such as the verification of indebtedness, which is covered in Section 3405. Caseworkers can use this section to ascertain how different types of property affect resource limits but should look elsewhere for policies on indebtedness verification or specific cases of unmarketable property not declared by authority.
3420: Section 3420 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the treatment of income for determining SNAP eligibility, categorizing income as either earned or unearned, and outlines how to consider sources such as wages, bonuses, and benefits from various programs. Key decision points for caseworkers include determining whether income is accessible and countable, jointly received incomes, and handling income exclusions or deductions, especially in situations of garnishment and bankruptcy. The section refers to Chart 3420.2 for specific types of income, using defined terminology such as "deemed income" and "ineligible ABAWDs," and relies on verification methods like pay stubs and Form 809 for validating incomes. Additionally, caseworkers should not use this section for policy on TANF assistance specifics or detailed treatment of child care costs, which are addressed in Sections 3210 and 3425, respectively. Hence, this section aids caseworkers in identifying countable income types and how to verify them but does not delve into detailed resource assessment or non-income-related benefits.
3425: Section 3425 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the treatment of self-employment income, detailing how income from a personal business, rather than a salaried position, should be calculated and verified. It covers specific policies for determining self-employment status, types of entities (e.g., partnerships, corporations, S-corporations, LLCs), and allowable expenses under a 40% standard deduction for business costs. Key forms include IRS documents like Form 1040, Schedule K-1, and others for verifying income. The section provides guidance on both annualized and non-annualized income computation and explains how to handle farm losses and boarder income, utilizing Chart 3425.1 and Chart 3425.2 for expense and income determination. Caseworkers should note that the section dictates income procedures but does not address scenarios involving changes in household composition or number of dependents, which are covered in Section 3610. This section aids in understanding the computation and verification of self-employment income but does not deal with general income or employment verification, which would be covered under different sections of the manual.
3430: Section 3430 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the treatment of various types of military pay when determining SNAP eligibility. It outlines that military pay, including housing and subsistence allowances, is generally considered earned income if the military individual is an AU member, and as unearned income if they are not but contribute financially to the AU. Procedures require verification of military income via the Leave and Earnings Statement (LES), and specific rules are provided for different types of military pay, as detailed in Chart 3430.1. Noteworthy exceptions include the exclusion of combat pay and clothing maintenance allowance from gross income calculations. This section should not be consulted for child support deductions or federal tax exclusions, which are covered in Section 3616. Caseworkers will find this section useful for understanding military-specific income treatments but should refer to other sections for general income and benefit exclusions.
3500: Section 3500 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the procedures and requirements for computer matches used to verify the eligibility and benefit levels of applicants and recipients. The policy mandates the comparison of the primary social security numbers (SSNs) of applicants and recipients with SSNs in governmental agency files to identify and investigate discrepancies through the Gateway system. Computer matches ensure proper benefit allocation and detect cases for potential legal action. Access to this information requires a valid user ID and password from the Gateway Security Unit, with all inquiries monitored for lawful access. Notably, information obtained for Unemployment Compensation Benefits (UCB) or Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) on interstate matches is considered verified. This section does not address procedures for manual verification processes or changes in household composition (see Section 3600). Caseworkers can use this section to understand the technical and procedural aspects of computer matches but must refer to other sections for issues like manual case adjustments or non-SSN-related verification protocols.
3505: Section 3505 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the procedures and requirements for using the Income and Eligibility Verification System (IEVS). Key topics include the use of federal and state data matches through Gateway to verify applicant and recipient data, with specific attention to matches involving the SSA Prisoner Verification Inquiry, SSA Death Verification Inquiry, Georgia Department of Corrections, and National Accuracy Clearinghouse. The section emphasizes the requirement to resolve discrepancies within 45 days and refers caseworkers to the Georgia Gateway Documentation Standards for documenting actions taken. It instructs caseworkers on verification processes for suspicious data such as DOL wage matches and prisoner or death verification data. This section does not cover procedures for appealing a benefit decision or fraud investigation protocols, which are addressed in other sections. Caseworkers seeking guidance on specific data matching processes, resolution timelines, and documentation requirements will find answers here, but should refer to Sections involving eligibility appeal rules for related issues beyond verification and data matching.
3510: Section 3510 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the National Accuracy Clearinghouse (NAC), implemented to prevent interstate duplicate participation in the SNAP program, as mandated by the Agriculture Improvement Act of 2018 and codified in 7 CFR § 272.18. This section outlines the requirements for using NAC during applications, recertifications, and when adding household members, as well as specifying expedited processing standards and procedures for resolving NAC matches. The policy defines terms such as "initiating state," "matching state," and "vulnerable individuals," and details the required actions and notifications, such as the "Notice of SNAP Participation Match In Another State." It includes Chart 3510.1 for processing NAC-related actions and specifies time limits, like the 10-day timeframe for resolving matches. This section does not address verification procedures unrelated to NAC (see Section 3035) or handling invalid matches outside the stated parameters. Caseworkers can rely on this section to resolve NAC matches and manage SNAP participation but must refer to other sections for general verification and non-NAC-related matters.
3515: Section 3515 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the use of the Clearinghouse system for accessing wage and benefit data from various agencies, crucial to SNAP eligibility decisions. Key topics include the timing of Clearinghouse access (e.g., at registration, finalization, and interim changes), and specific requirements for reviewing Georgia Department of Labor (DOL) wage files for individuals aged 16 and older at different stages such as initial application and renewal. Decision points involve verifying employment history, current employment status, reported wages, and need for fraud referral if income exceeds the 130% gross income ceiling (GIC). Specific tools include Chart 3515.1 and references to procedures in Section 3035 for verifying terminated income. This section addresses caseworker queries about when and how to access and use wage data but does not cover unrelated eligibility determination factors, such as childcare payments, found in other sections.
3520: Section 3520 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual discusses policies and procedures related to Prisoner Verification Inquiries (PVI) through interfaces with the Social Security Administration (SSA) and the Department of Corrections (DOC). It details the process for handling prisoner alerts, including decision points for when to send an individual's Social Security Number (SSN) for verification, and outlines the conditions under which alerts or tasks are generated, described by specific alert/task codes (11011, 11012, 11023, and 11049). The section includes time limits, such as the requirement to mail a Verification Checklist (VCL) within 10 days unless third-party verification is achieved. Charts 3520.1 and 3520.2 provide summaries of verification procedures, while notable conditions and decision points regarding AU composition thresholds and verification procedures are described. The section does not cover issues related to law enforcement actions; for those, see Section 3715 for when not to act on system-generated alerts. Caseworker questions addressed include steps for evaluating prisoner alerts and handling verification checklists but do not extend to enforcement of incarceration policies beyond SNAP eligibility.
3525: Section 3525 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the Social Security Administration (SSA) Death Verification Inquiry, detailing the process and requirements for verifying the deaths of AU members. It outlines the necessity for computer matches between SSA files of deceased individuals and SNAP applicants/recipients, highlighting that SSA information is not verified upon receipt. Key actions include sending a verification checklist within 10 days of receiving a task, and the removal of the deceased member from the AU at specific intervals (Intake, Renewal, Periodic Reporting, or Change). Caseworkers are to ensure that the AU is informed, and if no response is received within the timeframe, benefits are terminated with adequate notice. Notably, this section emphasizes contacting the AU before taking action and offers procedures for appointing a new primary individual if applicable. This policy section addresses procedures during intake and periodic reporting but refers to Section 3715 for managing interim changes when the primary individual dies or moves. It also instructs on overpayment creation and fraud referral to the Office of Inspector General (OIG). This section helps caseworkers understand the process for handling death matches reported by SSA but does not cover other verification methods found in Section 3035.
3530: This section, "3530 — Social Security Number (SSN) Validation," outlines the procedures for verifying SSNs of AU members through interfacing with the SSA and correcting discrepancies. Key processes include annotating SSNs with an FV (federally verified) code when validated and identifying mismatches in data or duplicate SSNs, which may require referral to SSA for resolution. The section introduces forms and procedures, such as the "FV code removal request" and steps for changing a validated SSN by contacting the empi.helpdesk@dhs.ga.gov. The section explicitly handles SSN validation, discrepancies, and corrections; it does not apply to non-SSN related identification issues (see Section 3520 for general identification verification). It resolves questions regarding SSN validation steps and error correction but does not address issues related to general eligibility criteria or non-SSN related demographic errors.
3600: Section 3600 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual focuses on the budgeting process required for determining financial eligibility for Assistance Units (AUs). Key topics include the prospective budgeting method, which involves estimating monthly income and expenses, and allowable deductions such as 20% earned income, standard, medical, dependent care, child support, and shelter deductions. Eligibility involves meeting the Gross Income Ceiling (GIC) and Net Income Limit tests. Documentation requirements include recording income, expenses, and sources of verification. This section answers questions about income calculation, deductions, and documentation for determining eligibility and benefit levels. It does not cover specific policies regarding asset limits (see Section 3500) or application/renewal procedures (see Section 3700).
3605: Section 3605 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual covers the rules and procedures for prospective budgeting, focusing on using representative income and expenses to determine eligibility and benefit amounts for an Assistance Unit (AU). It details how stable and fluctuating incomes and expenses are calculated, verified, and converted using specific conversion factors (4.3333 weekly, 2.1666 bi-weekly, 2 semi-monthly, and 1 monthly). Notably, verification of income prioritizes Truv as the primary source starting July 1, 2024, and involves using pay stubs, employer forms, or client statements as last resort options. The section provides minimum verification requirements for different payment frequencies (Chart 3605.1) and methodologies to calculate monthly income and expenses (Charts 3605.2 and 3605.3), emphasizing the non-use of non-representative periods. It cannot answer questions regarding child support deduction rules (refer to Section 3616) nor the overall policy on acceptable verification sources (refer to Section 3035). Caseworkers will find guidance on how to handle fluctuating incomes, changes in income and expenses, and relevant documentation procedures.
3610: Section 3610 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the budgeting procedures for determining the financial eligibility and benefit levels of Assistance Units (AUs). Key topics include income assessments using the Gross Income Ceiling (GIC) at 130% of the FPL and net income limits at 100% of the FPL, along with the exclusion criteria for gross income. The section provides a detailed step-by-step guide on completing a SNAP budget, including necessary deductions for calculating net income. Notable conditions include exceptions for AUs with elderly or disabled members exempt from the GIC test, and ineligible student's income not considered for eligibility. For determining the benefit amount, caseworkers refer to the Basis of Issuance Tables and Appendix A for financial standards. Caseworker questions on detailed earnings and deduction calculations are addressed here, while the resources of TANF, SSI, and TCOS recipient cases should refer to Section 3210.
3611: Section 3611 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the deductions applicable to an assistance unit's (AU's) income prior to determining financial eligibility and benefit levels. Key deductions include a 20% earned income deduction, standard deduction, excess medical, dependent care, child support, excess shelter, and homeless shelter deductions. Deductions are not permissible for expenses reimbursed or covered by vendor payments but are allowed for expenses paid with borrowed money. This section refers users to Section 3620, Section 3625, and Section 3635 for detailed policy on specific deduction situations. It is crucial for the expenses to be incurred or billed to the AU currently or on an ongoing basis, regardless of the AU's intent or ability to pay. Caseworker guidance provided here focuses on eligibility for deductions but does not cover policy specifics found in referenced sections.
3612: Section 3612 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the earned income deduction policy, which allows a 20% deduction on the total countable gross earned income for assistance units (AUs) with earned income. The deduction accounts for withholdings and work expenses. A crucial condition is the timely reporting of earned income, as failure to do so results in the loss of this deduction. This section does not cover the impact of self-employment income or unearned income deductions; those details are addressed in Section 3650. Caseworkers can find guidance on applying the 20% deduction, understanding eligibility criteria, and identifying applicable gross income. However, it does not address reporting requirements for changes in employment status, which can be found in another section.
3613: Section 3613 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the application of standard deductions from countable income for Assistance Units (AUs) based on size, effective from October 1, 2025, to September 30, 2026. The specific standard deductions are $209 for AUs with 1-3 members, $223 for AU size 4, $261 for AU size 5, and $299 for AUs with 6 or more members, aligning with the USDA FNS cost of living adjustments. This section addresses how to apply these deductions but does not cover the determination of AU size or eligibility criteria, which are detailed in Sections 3600 and 3700, respectively. It is crucial for caseworkers to understand that this section does not address income verification or reporting procedures, which are found in Section 3620. Caseworkers can rely on this section for guidance on deduction amounts and their application to total countable income but should refer to other sections for eligibility assessment and income documentation requirements.
3614: Section 3614 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual covers the Excess Medical Deduction for assistance units (AUs) with elderly or disabled members. It outlines conditions under which medical expenses exceeding $35 per month can be claimed, either through a Standard Medical Deduction (SMD) of $161 or actual medical expenses, if they exceed $196 monthly. Key forms and verifications include Form 840 for medical transportation and various methods for verifying expenses. Charts 3614.1 to 3614.3 aid in determining allowable costs and budgeting methods. The section also specifies that special diets and Schedule I controlled substances are not deductible expenses. This section helps caseworkers determine eligibility and documentations needed for the excess medical deduction but does not address recertification processes covered in Section 3710 or interim changes detailed in Section 3715.
3615: Section 3615 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the requirements and considerations for claiming the dependent care deduction. This deduction applies when an Assistance Unit (AU) member incurs expenses to search for or maintain employment, fulfill employment and training requirements, or pursue education related to employment. Key rules include allowing transportation costs and full expenses for children under 18 or any incapacitated person. However, deductions are not allowed for dependent care expenses paid to an AU member or covered by Title IV programs, like TCC and CAPS. Important verification can include receipts or statements from providers, with CAPS verification being primary. The section clarifies that educational expenses, such as books or tuition, do not qualify under dependent care. This section helps caseworkers determine eligibility for dependent care deductions but does not cover medical deduction eligibility or overlap, which is handled separately in Section 3360.
3616: Section 3616 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the rules and requirements for a child support deduction within the SNAP program, specifically when an Assistance Unit (AU) member is legally obligated to pay support for a child outside the AU. Key issues covered include verifying the legal obligation through court orders or administrative processes and documenting actual payment amounts over the most current three-month period using receipts, checks, and administrative records. Notably, past due child support can only be deducted if it is verified and not previously deducted, while alimony payments are not eligible for deduction under this policy. Verification is crucial at initial application, recertification, interim changes, periodic reporting, and when information is questionable, with references to additional sections like 3710, 3715, and 3730 for further details. This section aids caseworkers in determining eligibility and processing deductions but does not pertain to situations involving alimony (as noted) or other unrelated SNAP budgeting issues, which would likely be found in other sections of the manual.
3617: Section 3617 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual provides detailed guidelines on calculating shelter and utility deductions for Assistance Units (AUs), including the criteria for excess shelter deductions over 50% of the AU's income. Notably, AUs with members who are elderly or disabled may exceed the maximum standard deduction. Third-party verification of shelter expenses is mandatory starting July 1, 2024. Key thresholds include a maximum monthly shelter deduction of $744. Important terminology includes the Heating/Cooling Standard Utility Allowance (H/C SUA) of $405 and the Limited Standard Utility Allowance (LSUA) of $358. Relevant charts include Chart 3617.1 for allowable housing expenses and Chart 3617.3 for shared utility expenses. Caseworkers can use this section to determine eligibility for deductions and suitable allowances, but scenarios involving homeless shelters are covered in Section 3618, and verification questions should refer to Section 3035.
3618: Section 3618 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the Homeless Shelter Deduction, applicable for homeless households not receiving free shelter throughout the month. It sets a threshold for the deduction amount at $199 and explains its application conditions, noting that if allowable shelter expenses exceed this amount, households may qualify for the excess shelter deduction or standard utility allowance instead (refer to Section 3617). A household is defined as homeless if it meets criteria related to temporary or inadequate nighttime residences, with imminent homelessness defined as losing the residence within 14 days. Verification of shelter expenses via third-party sources is mandatory; without verification, deductions cannot be applied. This section helps caseworkers decide eligibility for the homeless shelter deduction but does not address budgeting decisions when telephone expenses are the household's only cost, directing such issues to Section 3617 instead.
3620: Section 3620 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses how to budget for an Assistance Unit (AU) with individuals who fail to comply with enumeration requirements. Key rules include excluding enumeration sanctioned individuals from the AU count for determining resource and income limits, while counting their resources fully toward other AU members. A pro rata share of the sanctioned individual’s income and expenses is included in the budgeting for eligible AU members, with guidelines for prorating or not prorating deductions based on who incurs the expenses. Procedures detail steps to compute income and benefits—including specific deductions, such as the 20% earned income deduction and the non-prorated standard deduction. This section specifically does not allow the excess medical deduction if the sanctioned individual is eligible, nor does it exceed the shelter/utility cap if the sanctioned individual alone qualifies for unlimited deductions. Caseworkers can use this section to determine income allocation and benefit levels but should consult Section 3630 for different sanction scenarios and exemption rules.
3625: Section 3625 covers the budgeting process for assistance units (AUs) with members who are disqualified due to Intentional Program Violations (IPVs), failure to meet work requirements, or being lawbreakers. It details the exclusion of these individuals from the AU when assessing resource and income limits, while counting their income after allowable deductions. Important procedures include calculating the AU's income, applying appropriate deductions, and notifying the AU of changes in benefit amounts and disqualification periods. The section emphasizes timely and adequate notification requirements, applying disqualifications from the month dictated by court orders or OPIC decisions, and prescribes steps for handling over issuances. Exclusions covered here do not address other disqualification types, which may be found in Sections 3315, 3310, and 3380. This section guides caseworkers on calculating benefits and implementing sanctions but not on unrelated eligibility inquiries.
3630: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the procedures for budgeting benefits for Assistance Units (AUs) with sponsored aliens. It covers the conditions under which a sponsor's income and resources are deemed to an alien's own income and resources, emphasizing the requirements for a legally binding affidavit of support (Form I-864 or I-864A). Key decision points include determining exceptions to deeming, such as battered individuals, sponsor and alien deaths, or indigent status, which must be reassessed every 12 months. The section provides detailed steps for calculating countable resources and income, and includes specific thresholds like the 130% Federal Poverty Level (FPL) for indigence. Notable exceptions covered are situations involving agency sponsorship and circumstances that result in the alien being ineligible. The procedures involve using specific forms such as INS Form G-845 for verification and a form letter to notify the U.S. Attorney General in the case of indigence. This section can answer questions about budgeting and eligibility in the context of sponsored aliens but does not address situations where aliens do not wish to disclose sponsor information (refer to Section 3635).
3635: Section 3635 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the budgeting process for Assistance Units (AUs) containing ineligible aliens, non-applicants, or ineligible Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs). This section outlines that while these individuals are excluded from the AU count for resource and income limits, their resources and a pro rata share of their income are considered in determining the eligibility of remaining AU members. Key procedures include calculating prorated income deductions and specific guidelines for expenses related to shelter, dependent care, and child support. Critical NOT HERE IF conditions reference Section 3320 for Citizenship/Alien Status decisions and Section 3355 for ABAWD criteria. Section 3635 can answer caseworker queries on income calculations and benefit levels but does not cover eligibility criteria for alien status or ABAWD classifications, which are found in their respective sections.
3640: Section 3640 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the budgeting of contract and self-employment income, detailing that annual income received over a period shorter than a year is averaged across 12 months unless paid hourly or by piecework. The section specifies contracts for occupations like truckers, school employees, sharecroppers, and farmers, and explains contract renewal processes. It establishes procedures for assessing the benefit level, including calculating monthly and annual gross income, applying deductions, and determining eligibility. Key details include the exemption from Employment & Training (E&T) during nonwork periods if average weekly earnings meet the federal minimum wage equivalent of thirty hours. Not applicable scenarios involve expedited processing during non-pay periods, deviations from contract payment terms, and labor disputes affecting earnings. This section helps caseworkers calculate income for contract employees but does not guide situations like hourly or piecework incomes, which may fall under Section 3650.
3650: Section 3650 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the failure to report earned income and its impact on budgeting overpayments. The key rule is that the earned income deduction is not permitted for earnings that are not reported in a timely manner, specifically affecting the calculation of overpayments. The section outlines that gross income changes exceeding 130% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) must be reported within 10 days after the month’s end when the income surpassed the Simplified Reporting Requirement (SRR). Additionally, actions must be taken within 10-14 days following this period for SRR Assistance Units (AUs). This section should not be used for queries related to asset limits or SNAP eligibility criteria, as those are addressed in Sections 3700 and 4300, respectively. Caseworkers will find guidance on determining overpayment months but will not find information on self-employment income, which is covered under Section 3670.
3700: Section 3700 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual encompasses the ongoing case management activities for Food Stamps once an Assistance Unit (AU) is approved. Key policy topics include the obligation for AUs to be notified about all case actions, cooperate with periodic eligibility reviews, and report any changes affecting eligibility or benefit levels, with all reported changes processed promptly. AUs are entitled to request hearings on case actions, and instances of reported changes necessitating benefit recovery refer to Volume IV, Benefit Recovery. This section does not address initial case application processes (refer to Section 3100), nor does it cover details on specific eligibility criteria or asset calculations, which might be found in earlier sections. Caseworkers will find this section useful for guidance on ongoing management protocols but should not look here for initial eligibility determinations or application procedures.
3704: Section 3704 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the Transitional Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (TSNAP), which provides benefits to SNAP assistance units (AUs) rendered ineligible for cash assistance due to employment-related income changes. Key requirements include eligibility criteria such as the necessity for the AU to have been TANF eligible for at least one month. TSNAP benefits are set at the current SNAP allotment level and extend for up to five months, starting from the month following TANF/RCA closure. Exclusions to TSNAP applicability, such as noncompliance with SNAP requirements, are specified, and a structured process with steps for determining TSNAP eligibility is detailed. Questions about TSNAP eligibility assessment can be answered here, but inquiries about regular SNAP procedures or specific sanction conditions should be referred to Section 3703. Forms such as the TSNAP Fact Sheet must be issued to notify AUs of their transitional benefits eligibility.
3705: Section 3705 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the requirements and procedures for notification to Assistance Units (AUs) concerning actions such as application approval/denial, benefit level changes, and eligibility determinations. The section mandates written notice, detailing the proposed action, reasons, effective month, and rights to a fair hearing, including conditions for continued benefits. Key forms include Form 333 for SNAP sanctions. It differentiates between "adequate notice" given concurrently with action and "timely notice," which involves a 14-day waiting period before the proposed action's implementation. This section does not address procedural questions related to appeals or hearings, which are covered in Appendix B. It clarifies actions requiring notification and remedies questions about notice procedures but excludes unrelated matters like food purchase restrictions (see Section 4100).
3710: Section 3710 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the recertification (renewal) process required to continue SNAP benefits. It details the types of renewals—timely, untimely, and late—and specifies time limits: timely applications are submitted by the 15th of the last month of the certification period. Key processes, such as reviewing all eligibility points, conducting interviews, obtaining verifications, and notifying applicants, are described. Notable forms include Form 508 and Form 297A; the section also references Chart 3710.1 for processing specifics. The manual excludes details on Periodic Reporting (Section 3730) and Senior SNAP policies (Section 3725). Caseworkers can find guidance on timelines, processing forms, and eligibility criteria here, but they should refer to other sections for managing periodic reports or the Senior SNAP program.
