3715: Section 3715 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses interim changes during the certification period, specifically focusing on the requirements for Assistance Units (AUs) under the Simplified Reporting Requirements (SRR). It outlines the conditions for reporting changes, such as when an AU's income exceeds 130% of the federal poverty level or an ABAWD's work hours fall below required levels. Key time limits include a 10-day period for reporting changes and providing verification. The section also details processing protocols for address and shelter changes, medical expense deductions, and expedited changes, while excluding scenarios requiring mass change processes (see Section 3500) or guidelines for adverse action notifications (see Section 3705). This section assists caseworkers with determining the timing and impact of reported changes on benefit levels but does not cover policy for mass change or automated adjustment processes.
3720: Section 3720 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the reporting requirements for SNAP assistance units (AUs) during the certification period, focusing on Simplified Reporting Requirements (SRR). It specifies that AUs must report changes like gross income exceeding 130% of the Federal Poverty Level, an ABAWD's work hours dropping below 20 per week, or substantial winnings of $4500 or more, all within ten calendar days of the month's end when the change occurs. Forms mentioned include Form 339 for SRR and Form 846 for reporting changes. Notably, caseworkers should reference Section 3355 for additional details on ABAWD work hour changes and Section 3730 for periodic reporting regulations. This section does not address actions related to prisoner matches or new hires, which appear in agency-required actions or notifications. Caseworkers can use this section to guide AUs on specific reporting timelines and verify reported changes but not to determine eligibility for Senior SNAP households, which defers to Section 3730.
3725: Section 3725 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the Senior Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (Senior SNAP), including eligibility criteria, verification requirements, and processing procedures. Critical rules include the age requirement for household members (65 years or older by May 1, 2026, with variations effective prior) and that all household members must have a fixed income with no earned income. Key forms referenced are the Senior SNAP application and renewal forms (Form 298 or 508), and the policy sets a 36-month certification period for eligible households. Notable exceptions are outlined, such as the requirement to cascade to regular SNAP if a household's composition changes or they no longer meet Senior SNAP criteria. This section does not address general verification requirements (see Section 3035) or budgeting policies (see Section 3610). Caseworker questions this section can answer include eligibility determination, necessary documents for verification, and procedures for initial applications and recertifications, but it cannot address issues related to regular SNAP, verification processes outside stated exceptions, or detailed budgeting rules.
3730: Section 3730 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual provides comprehensive guidance on periodic reporting for households receiving Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits. It details the requirements for households certified for periods longer than six months, specifying that periodic reports are due in the sixth month for 12-month certifications and in the 12th month for 24-month certifications. The section outlines the procedural steps for filing and processing periodic reports, including submission methods, verification requirements, and notification timelines, with forms like Form 528 and Form 859 being essential to the process. It emphasizes specific policy topics like changes in household circumstances impacting the reporting process, such as changes in income and ABAWD work requirements. This section does not cover recertification procedures or the adjustment of certification periods, which can be found in Section 3725. Caseworkers can refer to this section for guidance on processing periodic reports and understanding submission deadlines but should look elsewhere for recertification-specific queries or for expedited processing instructions, as this is not applicable to periodic reports.
3800: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual, Section 3800 — Issuance Overview, addresses the procedures and rules for distributing benefits to eligible food stamp assistance units (AUs) through EBT cards. Key policy topics include the authorized mailing addresses for EBT cards, such as the residential address, mailing address, a specific Post Office Box, or through General Delivery in certain situations. Noteworthy exceptions include the prohibition of mailing EBT cards "in care of" another person. The section details conditions under which different mailing addresses may be used, particularly for homeless or seasonal farmworker AUs, and emphasizes documentation of valid reasons for non-standard addresses. Caseworkers will find this section helpful in understanding the approved issuance methods and the documentation needed but will need to refer to other sections, such as eligibility verification requirements (Section 2300), for information on initial eligibility determinations.
3805: Section 3805 of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the issuance and management of Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) cards, including setting up accounts via the Gateway system, issuing cards, and processes for manual issuance when the system fails. It discusses key decision points such as voiding pending benefits, account expungement after 9 months of inactivity, and re-obligating benefits during emergencies. Important forms include EBT Form 4 for card receipt documentation and EBT Form 9 for manual issuance requests. This section sets thresholds like a 180-day period for stale benefits and outlines specific procedures for erroneous debits and card skimming incidents. Notably, it does not cover conditions for Disaster SNAP EBT cards (see Section 3806). Caseworkers can find information on replacing lost cards, reporting erroneous debits, but should refer to other sections for the creation of initial SNAP accounts and policies unrelated to EBT transactions.
3810a: Section 3810a of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the issuance of SNAP benefits via electronic funds transfer (EFT) using EBT cards and PINs. It outlines rules for different types of benefits, including initial, ongoing, and supplemental benefits, and specifies prohibited purchases like alcohol and tobacco. Prorating of initial month's benefits is guided by a chart (Chart 3810-1), which uses multiplication factors based on the application date. This section clarifies the posting schedule of regular monthly benefits based on the last two digits of the client ID number. Key terminology includes "Gateway," "Basis of Issuance Tables," and terms specifying who may prepare meals under SNAP benefits. Not included are scenarios involving manually issued benefits, which should be addressed in Section 3805. This section answers caseworker questions about benefit issuance timelines and calculations but not about manually issued benefits or case closures, which are handled elsewhere.
3810b: Section 3810b of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the policies and procedures for benefit restoration, supplemental benefits, and replacement of food destroyed due to disaster or misfortune. It details specific scenarios warranting restoration, such as agency errors or IPV disqualification reversals, with benefits restored for up to 12 months prior to the request or discovery of loss. It notes exceptions, such as offsetting restorations against unpaid claims unless initial allotments or replacements due to disaster apply. The section outlines time limits for reporting disasters (10 calendar days) and forms required, like the Food Loss Replacement Form (Form 841). Notably, it emphasizes conditions like power outages of 4+ hours for food replacement eligibility. This section does not address where general SNAP application questions are covered; see Section 2100a for eligibility queries. Caseworkers will find this section useful for understanding restoration and replacement protocols but should refer elsewhere for discovering general eligibility or application processing rules.
appendix-a-financial-standards-overview: The "Financial Standards Overview" section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual covers the determination of monthly benefit amounts for eligible Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Assistance Units (AUs), based on adjusted net monthly income against the Basis of Issuance (BOI) tables, detailed in Section 3610. It includes the annual update procedure for BOI tables and income eligibility limits, aligned with the Consumer Price Index and Federal Poverty Level standards. The Thrifty Food Plan (TFP) is outlined as the basis for calculating maximum monthly allotments for varying AU sizes. The section provides the most recent SNAP eligibility income limits, maximum allotment amounts, and BOI tables. It can address caseworker queries about income limits, benefit calculations, and BOI updates but refers questions regarding specific AU compositions and allowances to other sections. Queries about deductions and exemptions not covered in this overview should refer to Section 3610 for more detailed guidelines.
appendix-a-food-stamp-income-limits: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual primarily addresses the income limits necessary for SNAP eligibility, effective October 1, 2025, for 48 states and the District of Columbia. It specifies the Maximum Gross and Net Monthly Income thresholds, along with the Monthly Gross Income Limit for Elderly/Disabled individuals and Maximum Allotments, based on household size. Important decision points include how to determine a household’s SNAP allotment using the Basis of Issuance tables and manual calculation methods for larger households. Notably, the conditions for categorically eligible households and rounding rules for one and two-person households are detailed. This section does not address non-financial eligibility criteria, assistance for non-elderly disabled individuals beyond income considerations, or emergency SNAP benefits (refer to SECTION: emergency-snap-assistance for those topics). Caseworkers can use this section to understand eligibility based on income and benefits calculation but must refer elsewhere for comprehensive eligibility determination and expedited SNAP processes.
appendix-b-administrative-disqualificati: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual details the procedures and requirements for Administrative Disqualification Hearings (ADH) initiated by the Office of Inspector General (OIG) when an Intentional Program Violation (IPV) is suspected. Key topics include the scheduling, notification, and conduct of hearings by the Office of State Administrative Hearing (OSAH), as well as the conditions for postponement and consolidation of hearings with fair hearings. It specifies the hearing notice contents, how failure to appear is handled, and the issuance of hearing decisions, including disqualification periods and repayment obligations. The section also outlines the process for waiving an ADH and the implications of such a waiver. This section does not cover the general prosecution procedures or non-ADH-related fraud handling, which are found in Section 3315, Intentional Program Violations. It answers caseworker questions about the ADH process, timelines, and outcomes but does not address questions regarding non-fraud claims or unrelated fair hearing procedures.
appendix-b-final-appeals: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses the process and requirements for appealing initial hearing decisions through final judicial appeals, as outlined in House Bill (HB) 790. It details the steps that Assistance Units (AU) must follow to file a final appeal, including the submission of Form 136 and supporting documents for the judicial review in the appropriate Superior Court within 30 days of the initial decision notice. Key procedural steps involve obtaining clearance from the SNAP Policy Unit and coordinating with the Office of General Counsel. Chart B3 is crucial for determining the continuation, reinstatement, or adjustment of benefits during the appeal process. Important terms include "Final Appeal," "judicial review," and "Special Assistant Attorney General (SAAG)." This section does not cover scenarios involving initial eligibility determinations (see Sections 402 and 403) or administrative disqualification hearings for Intentional Program Violations (refer to Section 403). Caseworkers' questions about timelines and documents for appeals are answered here, but queries about initial eligibility decisions or IPV hearings must be referred to the relevant sections.
appendix-b-hearings-overview: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual, titled "Hearings Overview," outlines the procedures and rights associated with fair hearings for assistance units (AU) aggrieved by agency actions affecting SNAP participation. It details the entitlement to a hearing, emphasizing the AU's right to request one, either orally or in writing, and specifies that hearings are conducted by an Administrative Law Judge from the Office of State Administrative Hearings (OSAH). The section includes instructions on notification of hearing rights, handling non-English speakers, and representation at hearings, as well as procedures to withdraw or postpone a hearing. Important forms, such as the OSAH Form 1, time thresholds like the eight-working-day submission rule, and key charts, such as Chart B1, are highlighted. Notable exclusions include hearings for changes in SNAP issuance cycle—these are not covered in this section. It addresses specific caseworker inquiries, such as eligibility and procedures for initiating, withdrawing, or conducting hearings, but excludes topics like benefit issuance cycles, which are referenced elsewhere.
appendix-b-initial-hearings: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual, Appendix B: Initial Hearings, outlines the procedures and rights associated with requesting and conducting initial hearings for Assistance Units (AUs) disputing eligibility decisions or benefit levels. It specifies that an AU has 90 days from the notification date to request a hearing and describes expedited hearing procedures for special cases like seasonal farm workers. Important forms and documents include the OSAH Form and Chart B2, which addresses the continuation of benefits pending an initial decision. Caseworkers are informed on processing hearing requests, implementing decisions, and AU and agency rights during hearings, but should refer to other sections for scenarios like mass changes or specific disqualifications (e.g., IPV) not covered here. This section helps caseworkers understand AU rights, procedural steps, and how to manage disputes over benefit levels or eligibility but does not address broader SNAP eligibility criteria or ongoing benefit determination (see other manual sections like eligibility requirements).
appendix-b-responsibilities-of-ogc: The "Responsibilities of the OGC" section in the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual outlines the duties of the Office of General Counsel in relation to appeals of OSAH hearing decisions. This section specifically covers the roles of the OGC's appeals reviewer, including taking additional testimony, remanding cases to the Administrative Law Judge for corrections, and requesting responses to additional evidence. It emphasizes that the final decision depends on the ALJ record supplemented by new materials and mandates written notification to the AU about the final decision and their right to judicial review. Notably, this section does not cover scenarios involving initial hearing procedures or OSAH hearing rules, which are detailed in Section A-3. Caseworkers can refer to this for guidance on final appeal responsibilities but should consult different sections for procedural questions or initial hearing guidance.
appendix-b-responsibilities-of-the-offic: This section outlines the responsibilities of the Office of State Administrative Hearings (OSAH) regarding the conduct of hearings under Georgia SNAP policy, including providing a minimum of ten days written notice prior to hearings, the ability to change hearing schedules for good cause, and completing hearings within 60 days of the request. It details OSAH's authority to consolidate group hearings when only state or federal law is contested, hear cases involving TANF-related changes affecting SNAP benefits, and address newly emerged issues during proceedings. The section specifies that hearing decisions must adhere to federal laws, be based on evidence presented, and be public with confidentiality maintained. It excludes scenarios like subpoenaing medical review team members, directing those inquiries to specific sections about medical assessments and professional evaluations. Caseworkers can find guidance on procedural timelines, the scope of issues for hearings, and claimants' appeal rights here but should refer elsewhere for conditions regarding case eligibility or benefits calculation. The criteria and record-keeping duties of Administrative Law Judges are also explicitly defined.
appendix-d: Appendix D of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual addresses Case Record Maintenance and Document Management, detailing the requirements for maintaining electronic case files within the Web-Center Enterprise Capture (WEC) and Georgia's Gateway System. It specifies that case records are divided into Permanent Verification, Benefits Support, and Claims sections, each with distinct documentation requirements, including age and identity verifications, application forms, and claims-related documents. The policy mandates retention periods of three years for both active and inactive cases, with exceptions for eligibility-verifying documentation and disqualification-related materials, which are permanent. Notably, it highlights necessary document destruction processes for maintaining confidentiality and directs inquiries related to confidentiality, voter registration, and HIPAA to Sections 3005, 3010, and 3040, respectively. Caseworkers are guided on documentation filing and retention but must consult other sections for related voting registration and confidentiality policies.
appendix-e: The "appendix-e — Glossary" section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual defines specific terms and acronyms related to the SNAP, TANF, and Medicaid programs. It outlines key terminology, including work criteria for ABAWDs, time limits for SNAP eligibility, and Medicaid definitions such as ABD Medicaid and QMB. Important data interfaces and systems such as Gateway, BENDEX, and IEVS are also described. Additionally, this section defines terms related to the eligibility process, like “application” and “recertification,” and specifies employment programs like E&T and SNAP Works. Caseworkers can use this glossary to understand terminology used in processing benefits and determining client eligibility but should refer to sections like 3105 for application processing details or 3420 for handling foster care payments if further details are needed. This section does not cover specific procedural guidelines or eligibility criteria, which are found in other sections of the manual (e.g., Section 3105 or Section 3614).
appendix-j: This section, Appendix J, outlines the procedures for handling customer complaints within the Office of Family Independence (OFI) related to Georgia SNAP policies. It categorizes complaints into four types: discrimination or civil rights issues, alleged HIPAA or confidentiality violations, disputes over benefit levels or allotment amounts leading to hearing requests, and customer service or processing delays. The section specifies that complaints should be collected at all contact points (County Offices, Customer Contact Center, and Office of Constituent Services). Complaints specifically about civil rights must be referred to Section 3030, which details the civil rights complaint process. Caseworkers can use this section to address complaints related to customer service at the initial contact point or escalate unresolved issues to the DFCS Constituent Services Unit, but it does not address specific civil rights complaint procedures or timelines.
appendix-l: This section of the Georgia SNAP Policy Manual, Appendix L, focuses on the Child Support Services Glossary, defining key terms and concepts pertinent to child support enforcement and TANF cases. It outlines the roles and obligations of absent or non-custodial parents, custodial parents, and nonparent custodians, as well as providing clear definitions for terms including Arrears, B5 Payments, Gap Budgeting, IV-A and IV-D cases, and Paternity Establishment. The glossary also details specific programs and legal mandates, such as the Title IV-D requirements for child support policy, and key financial components like the Standard of Need (SON) and Unreimbursed Public Assistance (UPA). Important distinctions include the differences between IV-D and Non-IV-D child support, and the definition of "Maintenance-only payments" and "Unearned income." This section is not intended to address unrelated policy aspects such as SNAP benefit computation details (see Section 332-2) or Medicaid eligibility requirements (see Section 800). Caseworker questions related to establishing paternity, understanding child support obligations, and the integration of child support within TANF budgets can be effectively addressed using this glossary. However, queries regarding specific case management procedures or client-specific eligibility determinations should refer to related procedural sections.
